# Here we go again: Brewers advance to NLCS rematch with Dodgers

23 minutes ago

Adam McCalvy

SAN DIEGO – For the second straight year, the Brewers will play for the pennant. 

And for the second straight year, the Dodgers are standing in the way.

If this Milwaukee team really is different after winning a franchise-record 103 games in the regular season and taking down baseball’s hottest second-half team in the National League Division Series, which ended Wednesday with a 3-1 Brewers win over the Padres in Game 4 at Petco Park, then this is the time to show it. Milwaukee is moving on to the League Championship Series for the second straight season and the fifth time in franchise history. Their last three have been against the Dodgers.

Game 1 is Sunday at American Family Field, after the Dodgers finished off the Braves in four games earlier Wednesday. And if you’re wondering what’s different about this Brewers team compared to the others, it starts with this: Jacob Misiorowski will be on the mound.

The NL Cy Young Award frontrunner was in the bullpen for the start of Wednesday’s game in a sign of the urgency the Brewers carried into the night. If they could take the NLDS in four games, they would have Misiorowski primed and ready to throw the first pitch of the NLCS. But for that to become a reality, the Brewers had to rewrite the narrative that they cannot win a postseason game on the road. They had come up empty in each of their last 12 tries, tying for the longest road losing streak in the postseason in MLB history.

The last time they had won on the road in the playoffs? Game 3 of the 2018 NLCS, when they beat Walker Buehler at Dodger Stadium.

And who started for the Padres on Wednesday night? None other than Buehler.

The Brewers won the way they won games all year long, getting contributions from everywhere on the roster. 

It started with left-hander Robert Gasser, the onetime Padres prospect traded to Milwaukee in the Josh Hader deal in 2022, who’d missed most of the previous two seasons rehabbing from Tommy John surgery and didn’t crack Milwaukee’s Opening Day roster. He rose to the moment with four effective innings when it mattered most and departed with Milwaukee leading, 2-1. 

The runs came mostly from Garrett Mitchell, the former first-round Draft pick who battled four years of injuries before playing more games this season than his first four seasons combined, broke free from a 2-for-11, six-strikeout start to this series with an RBI single in third inning and a leadoff triple in the fifth that led to the go-ahead run. Jackson Chourio, the 22-year-old star in the making, lined a one-out single through a drawn-in infield for the 17th postseason RBI of his young career, passing Ryan Braun for the franchise record and matching Hall of Famer Andruw Jones for the most postseason RBIs in Major League history for a player shy of his 23rd birthday.

As of that moment, Chourio had driven in six of the Brewers’ first 12 runs in the series. 

By the time Sal Frelick’s sixth-inning sacrifice fly made it 3-1, the game belonged to the Brewers’ dynamic bullpen, starting with left-hander Aaron Ashby, whose uncle Andy pitched eight seasons for the Padres and made two All-Star teams. Ashby delivered three hitless innings to bridge the gap to Abner Uribe, facing the top of San Diego’s star-studded lineup while pitching for the fourth time in five days. He got through it, but not by much. Mitchell went all the way to Petco Park’s short center-field wall to catch what would have been a tying, two-run homer off the bat of Manny Machado for the second out of the inning, then saw second baseman Brice Turang make a tricky catch in foul ground to end the threat.

Padres lose 2026 NLDS to Brewers

# Padres left wondering what could have been after NLDS exit: 'It stings'

October 8th, 2026

AJ Cassavell

SAN DIEGO -- Every postseason exit hurts. They may hurt for different reasons. They all hurt.

This one, most of all, is going to hurt because of what could have been.

The Padres and Brewers staged an epic of a National League Division Series. The margins were thin. Agonizingly thin. A potential go-ahead home run off a cable on the roof in Milwaukee in Game 1. A Jackson Chourio line drive just beyond the outstretched glove of Jake Cronenworth in Game 2.

And maybe the cruelest of all: A potential game-tying, season-saving, bedlam-inducing home run from the bat of Manny Machado, taken away at the wall by Brewers center fielder Garrett Mitchell in Game 4.

Just like that, the Padres’ season was over. They dropped Game 4 of the NLDS to Milwaukee, 3-1, on Wednesday night at Petco Park. They lost the series by the same tally. So easily, it could have been different.

“It burns," said Machado. “It's pain. This team, we fought all year, dealt with a lot as a group. Overcame a lot. It stings right now, for sure. But at the same time, proud of these guys, what they've accomplished, what they've done, what we did this year -- a lot of great things. 

“Unfortunate. It just didn't go our way. But take the punch, and enjoy the ride that we had.”

This wasn’t 2024, when the Padres came apart in the two biggest games of their season. It wasn’t ‘25, when they fizzled, never quite reaching the gear you thought they might. These Padres could have beaten the Brewers. For years, San Diegans will swear that they should have.

They did not. For the first time in 111 years, a postseason series featured two teams that were never separated by more than two runs in any game. And the Padres came out on the losing end of it.

“It was a heavyweight battle,” said France. “They were the best team in baseball for a reason, and … we went punch-for-punch with them.”

The Padres weren’t making any excuses afterward, fully crediting the 103-win Brewers as deserving winners. Still, France and so many others will always believe, deep down, that his Game 1 fly ball would have been a go-ahead home run, had it not struck that cable. On Wednesday night, Brewers manager Pat Murphy wasn’t disputing that.

“The Padres, they’re a great team,” Murphy said. “They could have won it all, but that's just the postseason. The ball doesn't bounce your way. [Legendary late Brewers broadcaster Bob] Uecker knocks that ball down out of the rafters. And it's a different series. Chourio gets the hit off Miller, and it's a different series.

“So believe me, that team right there can beat anybody in baseball. I'm just grateful we got through.”

With time, the disappointment will be complemented by an appreciation that the Padres got here in the first place. Three games below .500 in late July, they stormed into the postseason with a scorching hot finish, then played six deeply memorable postseason games.

And yet, the wait goes on. There’s never been an era of Padres baseball quite like this one. They’ve reached the postseason in three straight years and five of seven. But this era still lacks its crowning achievement -- the first World Series title in franchise history.

“A lot to be proud of this year,” said manager Craig Stammen. “A lot to go home and say: ‘Yeah, we did a pretty good job.’ But also, we're not satisfied. We're not satisfied until we finally bring that championship to San Diego. But this year made us one step closer.”

An offseason full of questions lies ahead. The futures of Adrian Morejon, Ty France and Michael King are chief among those questions. In the aftermath of Wednesday’s defeat, all three expressed a desire to return.

# Brewers beat Padres in Game 4 to advance, set up NLCS rematch with Dodgers

By 

The Canadian Press

Published: October 08, 2026 at 1:08a.m. EDT

SAN DIEGO (AP) — Garrett Mitchell tripled and scored the tiebreaking run in the fifth inning before making a pivotal catch on Manny Machado’s drive to the wall in the eighth, and the Milwaukee Brewers advanced to the National League Championship Series for the second straight season with a 3-1 victory over the San Diego Padres on Wednesday night, winning their best-of-five Division Series in four games.

Mitchell also drove in Sal Frelick with Milwaukee’s first run as the Brewers snapped their 12-game postseason road losing streak since 2018 and reached the team’s fifth League Championship Series.

Machado nearly tied Game 4 with a 406-foot drive off reliever Abner Uribe, but Mitchell coolly tracked it down and reached just above the short wall in right-center to keep it in the yard. 

Second baseman Brice Turang then ended the eighth with an acrobatic catch of Ty France’s tailing popup in foul ground.

After fending off the surging Padres in four tight games decided by a combined five runs, the 103-win Brewers will get an NLCS rematch with the Los Angeles Dodgers, who eliminated Atlanta on Wednesday.

The Dodgers swept Milwaukee last October on the way to their second consecutive World Series title.

Fernando Tatis Jr. hit a 429-foot homer on an otherwise tepid offensive night for the Padres, who repeatedly tested the majors’ best regular-season team before falling short of only the fourth NLCS appearance in team history.

One night after the Padres avoided elimination in Game 3, Milwaukee claimed its first road playoff win since the 2018 NLCS by sticking to its season-long formula for success.

While four Brewers pitchers combined on a three-hitter and the defense made nearly every big play, Milwaukee’s lineup calmly worked counts, pounded 10 hits through the Padres’ defense and manufactured enough runs to head home smiling.

Game 2 hero Jackson Chourio capped his high-impact series by driving in Mitchell to become the Brewers’ career leader in postseason RBIs at just 22 years old. Chourio has 17 RBIs, including six in this series, in 16 playoff games.

Milwaukee opened the scoring in the third when Frelick reached on an infield single, stole second and came around on a single by Mitchell, an Orange County native and UCLA product.

Brewers starter and former Padres draft pick Robert Gasser threw four innings of three-hit ball, but Tatis ended his 1-for-19 skid since San Diego’s playoff opener with a long shot to center in the third. It was the longest homer ever hit in the postseason at Petco Park by a San Diego player.

Padres starter Walker Buehler yielded just three hits and a run, but manager Craig Stammen replaced him with Game 1 starter Robbie Ray after William Contreras’ leadoff single in the fourth.

Mitchell then stroked a mild liner perfectly over first base and into the right-field corner leading off the fifth, and he scored on Chourio’s single through the drawn-in infield. Chourio surpassed Ryan Braun for the most postseason RBIs in Brewers history.

Jake Bauers singled leading off the sixth and went to third on Cooper Pratt’s ground-rule double before scoring on Frelick’s sacrifice fly.

The Padres were already down 3-1 in the seventh when Mason Miller allowed three baserunners, but no runs. The vaunted closer missed Game 3 for the birth of his first child.

After sitting below .500 and in 11th place in the NL in late July, San Diego roared into the first wild-card spot and then swept the Cubs in the Wild Card Series last week. The Padres had won 19 of 22 before losing three of four to Milwaukee.

Up next

Game 1 featured leading Cy Young Award contender Jacob Misiorowski starting for the Brewers against a former winner of the trophy in the American League in Robbie Ray. The Padres had a very simple plan heading into the contest: drive up Misiorowski's pitch count to force him out of the game early and take their chances against the rest of the Brewers' staff. The plan worked perfectly - except that San Diego was unable to score against any one other than the Miz in spite of a number of opportunities, and was ultimately thwarted by an overhanging wire as Milwaukee came up with a 3-2 win. 

Manny Machado hit a two-out double for San Diego in the top of the 1st, showing that Misiorowski was not completely unhittable, but he was stranded on base. After Ray retired the Brewers in order in the bottom of that inning, the 2nd inning proved much more successful for the Friars, as a series of small pokes led to two runs and forced Milwaukee's starter to throw a ton of pitches. Xander Bogaerts opened things with a one-out single, which was followed with back-to-back singles by Ethan Salas and Luis Campusano, leading to a first run. Jake Cronenworth then hit a ball to 1B Jake Bauers, who tried to cut off Salas at home plate, but his throw got away from C William Contreras and a second run scored, both runs coming courtesy of the bottom four men in the batting order. After a ground out by Fernando Tatis Jr. advanced the two runners to second and third base, Misiorowski walked Dustin Harris to load the bases and finally got out of the inning when Machado grounded out to short. No one expects to put up a crooked number by stringing a number of hits against the stingiest pitcher around, but it was exactly what San Diego had managed to do to take that two-run lead. Ray, who had been sitting around a long time, then gave up a single to Christian Yelich in the bottom of the inning, but nothing else. In the 3rd, however, Garrett Mitchell led off with a single and after moving to second on a ground out, he could jog he rest the way as Jackson Chourio sent a ball into the left-center field stands for a game-tying two-run homer. results.author: Patrick McAvoy

The Good, Bad, and Ugly From Brewers NLDS Series Win Over Padres

# The Good, Bad, and Ugly From Brewers NLDS Series Win Over Padres

The Milwaukee Brewers are moving on, but let's take a look back before the NLCS. 

Patrick McAvoy|

Sep 8, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Milwaukee Brewers designated hitter Christian Yelich (22) celebrates as Milwaukee Brewers left fielder Jackson Chourio (11) (not pictured) hits a two run home run to tie the game against the Chicago Cubs in the ninth inning at American Family Field. Mandatory Credit: Michael McLoone-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

In this story:

The Milwaukee Brewers took care of business in the National League Division Series against the San Diego Padres, despite the fact that the series was close throughout. 

In fact, neither the Brewers, nor the Padres, ever led a game by more than two runs. Still, the Brewers played their game and found ways to win baseball games. Despite how close the series was, the Brewers won three of four. It's just what the Brewers do. They find a way and it's why they won 103 games in the regular season and their fourth straight National League Central title. Now, they advance to the National League Championship Series with a trip to the World Series on the line.

It was a good series for the Brewers, of course, although there is room for growth. Now that it's over, let's break down the good, the bad and the ugly. 

## Jackson Chourio/William Contreras/Sal Frelick/Christian Yelich

Oct 4, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Milwaukee Brewers outfielder Jackson Chourio (11) grounds out during the ninth inning against the San Diego Padres in game two of the NLDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at American Family Field. Mandatory Credit: Michael McLoone-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

These four powered the Brewers' offense throughout the four-game series. While Chourio's batting average throughout the series wasn't good, he hit a home run, drove in six runs and had the walk-off winner in Game 2. Contreras was great all around and crushed two homers. Yelich batted .357 in the series and Frelick batted .333. 

## The Rotation

Oct 3, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Jacob Misiorowski (32) reacts after pitching in the fourth inning against the San Diego Padres in game one of the NLDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at American Family Field. Mandatory Credit: Michael McLoone-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

Jacob Misiorowski, Logan Henderson, Dustin May and Robert Gasser gave the club a chance to win each time out. That's all you can ask for in the playoffs. 

## The Bullpen

Oct 7, 2026; San Diego, California, USA; Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Trevor Megill (29) pitches during the ninth inning against the San Diego Padres in game four of the NLDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Petco Park. Mandatory Credit: David Frerker-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

The bullpen was even better and actually is leading the league with a 0.47 postseason ERA so far, despite tossing 19 innings throughout the four-game series. The bullpen got a lot of action and was phenomenal. 

## Brice Turang/Jake Bauers Offensively

Oct 7, 2026; San Diego, California, USA; Milwaukee Brewers second baseman Brice Turang (2) forces San Diego Padres first baseman Ty France (25) out at second and turns a double play during the sixth inning in game four of the NLDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Petco Park. Mandatory Credit: Denis Poroy-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

Neither Turang nor Bauers were able to get it going offensively against the Padres. Turang went 2-for-16 in the series and Bauers went 3-for-12. If the Brewers want to get through the two-time reigning champs, they need more from these two.
